title: LiveWorld — A design brief the world can check
disclosures: Actual application screenshots and native 30 fps simulation replay exports
Receipt, household, sensitivity and report frames are the running studio or its exported report
One previously observed AI-generated tabletop input and its recorded rescan
Recorded Meta contract translation, refusal and playtest, independently recomputed
Authored showcase, not a held-out benchmark or physical-camera test
Inference waiting time omitted; generic synthetic English narration

scenes.heading: The same total can hide a very different game.
scenes.caption: Same synthetic world · 20/24 on time in both · one home gets nothing · the other gives every home at least 3
scenes.narration: Twenty deliveries on time, in both worlds. One home gets nothing. The other gives every home at least three.

scenes.heading: Say the rule. Confirm it. Or get a refusal.
scenes.caption: Recorded translation of the 20/3/10 brief · recorded refusal of a request to add a courier · nothing applied
scenes.narration: The creator asks for twenty on time, three at every home, and at most ten turns of waiting. Muse Spark writes the contract. The creator confirms it. Ask for another courier, and Muse Spark refuses the whole request. The workers stay locked.

scenes.heading: A shorter queue can hide a losing household.
scenes.caption: Moved stick · waiting 22 to 10 · total stays 20/24 · four late units move onto one home · brief fails
scenes.narration: Moving the lower stick cuts waiting from twenty-two turns to ten. The total stays twenty of twenty-four. Four late deliveries move onto another home. That home gets nothing on time. The brief fails.

scenes.heading: The late trip is on the map.
scenes.caption: Receipt for one home · arrival at turn 84 · four turns late · courier-1 highlighted
scenes.narration: Select the late arrival. It reaches the home at turn eighty-four, four turns late. The courier lights up on the map. The receipt names the bridge and the simulator events.

scenes.heading: One cell breaks the passing layout.
scenes.caption: Lower bridge moved one cell in both worlds · nominal passes · both neighbors fail the same brief
scenes.narration: Move the lower bridge by one cell. Waiting breaks the cap in one direction. On-time deliveries break it in the other. The passing layout has a boundary.

scenes.heading: Save the test. The engine still decides.
scenes.caption: Tang Vu · Meta reads the request · the simulator scores it · generated tabletop · A fails and B passes
scenes.narration: Save the project and open it again. The brief and the measurements come back, recomputed. LiveWorld was built by Tang Vu. Meta reads the request. The simulator decides. This demo uses a generated tabletop.
